graph28_runtime_clock_activation.method: For each received nonzero-packet relay SR, enumerate original same-source-track SRs logged no later than receipt. Each defines a half-open interval for fixed C under exact integer NTP->RTP extrapolation at negotiated 48kHz audio/90kHz video, with signed modulo32 RTP delta. Intersect the union of allowed intervals for every report across both tracks. The first surviving interval midpoint predicts each relay RTP exactly; witnesses retain a matching preceding original SR. This is an observational consistency proof, not direct internal state telemetry or uniquely identified per-report source-anchor selection. Browser logger omits SDES; no wire-CNAME text claim.
limits: A shared fixed offset is consistent with every observed report, but runtime internal C values and selected individual source anchors are not directly logged. Matching original source anchors precede receipt, not necessarily relay emission; source-to-relay arrival timestamps are unavailable.

Chrome eventlog strips SDES, so no direct wire CNAME text claim. Given strict source-clock suppression/activation policy in the reviewed graph, nonzero incoming SRs plus exact shared-C consistency support authoritative runtime activation.
